title: Lalita Kumari v. Govt. of U.P.

content.caseIdentity: Lalita Kumari v. Govt. of U.P., (2014) 2 SCC 1
content.facts: The Constitution Bench considered the statutory duty to register information relating to a cognizable offence under Section 154 CrPC and the limited circumstances in which a preliminary enquiry may precede registration.
questionsBeforeCourt: Whether registration of an FIR is mandatory when information discloses commission of a cognizable offence and when a preliminary enquiry may be permissible.
content.ratioDecidendi: Registration of FIR is mandatory under Section 154 CrPC when the information discloses commission of a cognizable offence; a preliminary enquiry is permissible only in the limited categories identified by the Constitution Bench.
content.holding: Registration of FIR is mandatory under Section 154 CrPC when the information discloses commission of a cognizable offence; a preliminary enquiry is permissible only in the limited categories identified by the Constitution Bench.
content.relevance: Rule of mandatory FIR registration and strict guidelines on preliminary enquiry.

sources.evidenceNote: Official Supreme Court Reports material identifies Lalita Kumari in the Court's SCR corpus; an official Supreme Court judgment dated 28 April 2025 quotes the Constitution Bench's conclusion that registration of FIR is obligatory when information discloses a cognizable offence.
Official subsequent Supreme Court judgment reproduces and applies paragraph 97 of Lalita Kumari concerning obligatory FIR registration.
